read_to_string.title: How read_to_string works on a Cursor
read_to_string.description: Reads everything that is left into a String.

slides.caption: The bytes must be valid UTF-8, otherwise you get an error.
For files, std::fs::read_to_string(path) does it in one call.

new.title: How BufReader::new works
new.description: Adds a buffer to a reader, so small reads do not hit the source every time.

slides.caption: Besides speed, BufReader gives you the BufRead methods: lines, read_line, split.
Always wrap a File in a BufReader before reading it line by line.

lines.title: How BufRead::lines works
lines.description: An iterator over the lines of a reader, without the line endings.

title.text: for line in reader.lines() { let line = line?; ... }

slides.caption: "three", the last line without a newline.
Reading a file line by line: BufReader::new(File::open(p)?).lines().

read_line.title: How BufRead::read_line works
read_line.description: Reads one line, including its newline, and appends it to a String.

slides.caption: It returns the number of bytes read; 0 means the end was reached.
3 bytes are read: h, i and \n.
Call line.clear() before reusing the String, and trim() to drop the newline.

split.title: How BufRead::split works
split.description: Splits a reader's bytes at a delimiter byte.

slides.caption: Like lines, but with any delimiter, and the pieces are bytes.
The delimiter is not included in the pieces.

read_until.title: How BufRead::read_until works
read_until.description: Reads bytes up to and including a delimiter.

slides.caption: k, e, y and = are read.
Returns 0 at the end of the input.

bytes.title: How Read::bytes works
bytes.description: An iterator over the bytes of a reader, one at a time.

slides.caption: Simple, but slow on unbuffered readers: wrap files in a BufReader first.
Each byte can fail (e.g. a disk error), hence the Result.

take.title: How Read::take works
take.description: A reader that stops after n bytes.

slides.caption: Protects against reading too much, e.g. from the network.
The rest stays unread in the inner reader.

chain.title: How Read::chain works
chain.description: Reads one reader to the end, then continues with another.

slides.caption: The two readers behave as one.
Useful to put a header in front of a body.

read_exact.title: How Read::read_exact works
read_exact.description: Fills a buffer completely, or fails.

slides.caption: read() may return fewer bytes; read_exact keeps reading until the buffer is full.
Enough data: the buffer is filled.
The tool for fixed-size binary headers.

read_to_end.title: How Read::read_to_end works
read_to_end.description: Reads every remaining byte into a Vec<u8>.

slides.caption: Like read_to_string, but for any bytes.
std::fs::read(path) does this for a whole file.

write_all.title: How Write::write_all works
write_all.description: Writes the whole buffer, retrying until every byte is out.

slides.caption: write() may write only part; write_all loops until everything is written.
The bytes are handed to the writer.
Use write! / writeln! for formatted text.

flush.title: How Write::flush works
flush.description: Pushes buffered data out to its destination now.

l2.text: flush() sends it to the terminal

slides.caption: Standard output is line-buffered: text without a newline waits.
Without a newline it stays there.
flush makes it appear before reading input.
BufWriter also needs flush (or drop) before its data is written.

vec_write-write_all.title: How write_all works on a Vec<u8>
vec_write-write_all.description: Appends bytes to the end of the Vec.

slides.caption: Writing to a Vec<u8> never fails; it just grows.
Handy for building binary data or capturing output in tests.

vec_write-flush.title: How flush works on a Vec<u8>
vec_write-flush.description: Does nothing: a Vec has no buffer to empty.

slides.caption: Generic code calls flush on every writer; for a Vec it is a no-op.
The bytes are already in the Vec.
Files and stdout are where flush matters.

bufwriter-new.title: How BufWriter::new works
bufwriter-new.description: Collects small writes in memory and sends them out in big blocks.

slides.caption: Writing a file byte by byte is slow; BufWriter batches the work.
Small writes go into an 8 KB buffer.
The buffer is written when full, on flush, or on drop.
Call flush() at the end to see write errors; drop ignores them.

copy.title: How io::copy works
copy.description: Copies everything from a reader into a writer.

slides.caption: It reads chunks and writes them until the reader is empty.
Copy a download to a file, or a file to stdout.

stdin-read_line.title: How Stdin::read_line works
stdin-read_line.description: Reads one line typed by the user, including the newline.

slides.caption: The program waits until the user presses Enter.
trim() drops the newline so parse works.
Forgetting trim() is the classic reason parse fails on input. (The check simulates the typing.)

stdin-lines.title: How Stdin::lines works
stdin-lines.description: An iterator over the lines typed by the user (or piped in).

title.text: for line in io::stdin().lines() { total += line?.parse::<i32>()?; }

slides.caption: Ends when the input ends (Ctrl+D / Ctrl+Z, or the end of a piped file).
echo "3\n4" | cargo run feeds it from the shell. (The check simulates the input.)

with_capacity.title: How BufReader::with_capacity works
with_capacity.description: A BufReader with a buffer of the size you choose.

slides.caption: The default is 8 KB; large sequential reads may benefit from more.

capacity.title: How BufReader::capacity works
capacity.description: The size of the internal buffer.

slides.caption: Not how much data is buffered, but how much fits.
buffer() shows the data currently held.

buffer.title: How BufReader::buffer works
buffer.description: The data read ahead but not yet consumed.

slides.caption: After a read-ahead, part of the data waits in the buffer.
The buffer is filled; 6 bytes consumed.
Useful for protocol parsers that need to look ahead.

get_ref.title: How BufReader::get_ref works
get_ref.description: A reference to the reader inside.

slides.caption: The inner reader may be ahead of what you consumed, because of buffering.
After one read, the buffer pulled everything.
The inner Cursor is at the end: 3.
Do not read from the inner reader directly; buffered data would be skipped.

get_mut.title: How BufReader::get_mut works
get_mut.description: A mutable reference to the reader inside.

slides.caption: Changing the inner reader can confuse the buffer.
Prefer Seek on the BufReader itself, which discards the buffer correctly.

into_inner.title: How BufReader::into_inner works
into_inner.description: Unwraps the BufReader; buffered data is lost.

slides.caption: Anything already pulled into the buffer is discarded.
You get the inner reader back.

seek_relative.title: How BufReader::seek_relative works
seek_relative.description: Moves the position by an offset, keeping the buffer when possible.

slides.caption: Small skips stay inside the buffer, so nothing is reread.
Seek::seek would throw the buffer away.

bufwriter-with_capacity.title: How BufWriter::with_capacity works
bufwriter-with_capacity.description: A BufWriter with a buffer of the size you choose.

slides.caption: Writes are collected until the buffer is full.

bufwriter-capacity.title: How BufWriter::capacity works
bufwriter-capacity.description: The size of the internal buffer.

slides.caption: How much can be collected before a real write happens.

bufwriter-buffer.title: How BufWriter::buffer works
bufwriter-buffer.description: The bytes written but not yet passed to the inner writer.

slides.caption: They are sent on flush, when the buffer fills, or on drop.
get_ref() is still empty at this point.

bufwriter-get_ref.title: How BufWriter::get_ref works
bufwriter-get_ref.description: A reference to the writer inside.

slides.caption: Data reaches the inner writer only on flush.
Do not write to the inner writer directly.

bufwriter-get_mut.title: How BufWriter::get_mut works
bufwriter-get_mut.description: A mutable reference to the writer inside.

slides.caption: Bytes still in the buffer are not affected.
Flush, then clear the inner Vec.

bufwriter-into_inner.title: How BufWriter::into_inner works
bufwriter-into_inner.description: Flushes and returns the inner writer.

slides.caption: Returns an error if the final flush fails, with the BufWriter still inside.
Dropping a BufWriter also flushes, but ignores errors.

into_parts.title: How BufWriter::into_parts works
into_parts.description: Unwraps without flushing: the inner writer and the unwritten bytes.

slides.caption: Useful when the inner writer is broken and you want the data back.
pending is Err if a previous write panicked.

linewriter-new.title: How LineWriter::new works
linewriter-new.description: A buffered writer that flushes after every newline.

slides.caption: Complete lines go out at once; a partial line waits.
stdout uses line buffering like this.

linewriter-with_capacity.title: How LineWriter::with_capacity works
linewriter-with_capacity.description: A LineWriter with a chosen buffer size.

slides.caption: Very long lines are flushed when the buffer fills.

linewriter-get_ref.title: How LineWriter::get_ref works
linewriter-get_ref.description: A reference to the writer inside.

slides.caption: Without a newline nothing has been passed on yet.

linewriter-into_inner.title: How LineWriter::into_inner works
linewriter-into_inner.description: Flushes and returns the inner writer.

slides.caption: The partial line is flushed first.

linewriter-get_mut.title: How LineWriter::get_mut works
linewriter-get_mut.description: A mutable reference to the writer inside.

io-read_to_string.title: How io::read_to_string works
io-read_to_string.description: Reads everything from a reader into a new String.

slides.caption: A one-liner for any reader, including stdin.
The reader is read to the end.

stdout.title: How io::stdout works
stdout.description: A handle to the standard output stream.

slides.caption: Lock it for many writes in a row.

stderr.title: How io::stderr works
stderr.description: A handle to the standard error stream.

slides.caption: Messages go to the error stream.
Keeps errors separate from normal output when piping.

stdin.title: How io::stdin works
stdin.description: A handle to the standard input stream.

slides.caption: The check only takes the handle, without reading.

lock.title: How Stdout::lock works
lock.description: Locks standard output for a series of fast writes.

slides.caption: println! locks for every call; locking once is much faster in loops.
Other threads wait while you hold it.

stderr-lock.title: How Stderr::lock works
stderr-lock.description: Locks standard error for several writes.

slides.caption: Other threads cannot interleave their messages with yours.

stdin-lock.title: How Stdin::lock works
stdin-lock.description: Locks standard input, giving a BufRead with all its methods.

slides.caption: Use lines(), read_line(), and so on.
The check only takes the lock, without reading.

pipe.title: How io::pipe works
pipe.description: An OS pipe: bytes written to one end can be read from the other.

slides.caption: Often handed to child processes as stdin or stdout.
It comes out of the other.
Dropping the writer makes the reader see end-of-file.

from_raw_os_error.title: How io::Error::from_raw_os_error works
from_raw_os_error.description: An io::Error for an operating-system error number.

slides.caption: Code 2 means "not found" on both Unix and Windows.
Used when calling OS functions directly.

last_os_error.title: How io::Error::last_os_error works
last_os_error.description: The most recent error reported by the operating system on this thread.

slides.caption: Only meaningful right after an OS call that failed.
The buffered data is not lost: it is still inside the error.

into_error.title: How IntoInnerError::into_error works
into_error.description: Throws away the writer and keeps only the io::Error.

slides.caption: Handy with ? in functions returning io::Result.

into_inner_error-into_inner.title: How IntoInnerError::into_inner works
into_inner_error-into_inner.description: Gives back the BufWriter, still holding its unwritten data.

into_inner_error-into_parts.title: How IntoInnerError::into_parts works
into_inner_error-into_parts.description: Splits into the io::Error and the BufWriter.

slides.caption: Log the error, keep the data.
into_inner and into_error take one each.

writer_panicked-into_inner.title: How WriterPanicked::into_inner works
writer_panicked-into_inner.description: Recovers the buffered bytes after the inner writer panicked.

slides.caption: BufWriter::into_parts reports a panicked writer this way.

try_clone.title: How PipeWriter::try_clone works
try_clone.description: A second writer for the same pipe.

note.text: e.g. stdout and stderr of a child

slides.caption: The reader sees EOF only after every writer is dropped.
Common when a child gets both stdout and stderr.

pipe_reader-try_clone.title: How PipeReader::try_clone works
pipe_reader-try_clone.description: A second reader for the same pipe.

slides.caption: Bytes go to whichever reader reads first.
Each read takes the data out of the pipe.
